chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man bought a sacrificial offering, and it had a defect, one-eyed or otherwise, so he said:
If he has already paid its price, then it has sufficed for him. But if he has not paid its price, he should return it and buy another in its place.

The proper way to understand this report is what we mentioned regarding the first report: that it is to be understood as applying to the obligatory sacrificial offering, not the voluntary one. It is also possible that it is to be understood as indicating a kind of recommendation rather than obligation.

key_terms.أَجْزَأَ عَنْهُ: it sufficed and fulfilled the required duty for him
key_terms.عَيْبٌ: a defect or blemish affecting the animal
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering designated for hajj rites

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person buys a hady animal and later finds a defect in it?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling on a sacrificial animal for hajj when a defect is discovered in it. If its price has already been paid, it suffices; otherwise, it should be returned and replaced. The compiler explains that this is to be understood either in relation to the obligatory hady specifically, or as a recommendation rather than a binding obligation.
